Checking geometry and derivatives

Source: vignettes/checking-derivatives.Rmd
checking-derivatives.Rmd

A diagnostic checks a mathematical identity at sampled points. Repeat it at several interior points, and inspect the errors rather than treating a passing result as a proof over the whole manifold.

M <- manifold.sphere(3)
x <- torch_tensor(c(0.6, 0.8, 0), dtype=torch_float64())
u <- torch_tensor(c(-0.8, 0.6, 0), dtype=torch_float64())
P <- riem.problem(M, function(x) -x[1])
riem.check.manifold(M,x,u)$checks
#>                    check        error    tolerance status note
#> 1         metric_duality 7.818619e-17 0.0003162278   pass     
#> 2        metric_symmetry 0.000000e+00 0.0003162278   pass     
#> 3        positive_metric 0.000000e+00 0.0000000000   pass     
#> 4     tangent_membership 0.000000e+00 0.0000000000   pass     
#> 5 retraction_feasibility 0.000000e+00 0.0000000000   pass     
#> 6  retraction_derivative 5.000005e-06 0.0003162278   pass
riem.check.gradient(P,x,u)$curves
#>           step        error    slope
#> 1 1.000000e-01 2.580661e-03       NA
#> 2 1.930698e-02 1.089186e-04 1.924480
#> 3 3.727594e-03 4.147725e-06 1.987009
#> 4 7.196857e-04 1.552351e-07 1.997548
#> 5 1.389495e-04 5.791020e-09 1.999529
#> 6 2.682696e-05 2.158980e-10 1.999909
#> 7 5.179475e-06 8.048054e-12 1.999981
#> 8 1.000000e-06 3.000053e-13 1.999987
riem.check.hessian(P,x,u)$checks
#>               check        error   tolerance status note
#> 1 hessian_linearity 2.758348e-17 0.001581139   pass     
#> 2  hessian_symmetry 0.000000e+00 0.001581139   pass     
#> 3    hessian_taylor 4.067080e-09 0.001581139   pass

The gradient Taylor remainder should decay quadratically until roundoff intervenes. A Hessian Taylor test requires an exponential map or a declared second-order retraction. Without one, the Taylor test is inconclusive while linearity and symmetry tests still run.

bad <- riem.problem(M,function(x) -x[1],rgrad=function(x) x*0)
stopifnot(riem.check.gradient(bad,x,u)$status == "fail")
Q <- riem.problem(manifold.euclidean(3),function(x) (x*x)$sum())
riem.hessian.spectrum(Q,torch_ones(3,dtype=torch_float64()))$values
#> [1] 2
riem.devices(operations="basic")
#>   device type index available compatible

Spectrum results are Ritz estimates with residuals, not certificates that no unseen more extreme eigenvalue exists. Device probes qualify specific operations; unknown user callbacks retain the conservative full probe.
